content:
The image shows a dried, shriveled leaf that is dark brown to black in color. The leaf has a withered appearance and appears to have died back from the tip towards the base. This progressive death of the plant tissue, starting from the tip and moving downwards, is characteristic of Die-Back disease.

There are no signs of a powdery white substance (Powdery Mildew), sooty or black mold-like growth on the surface (Sooty Mould), or the distinct sunken lesions or spots typical of Anthracnose. The most fitting diagnosis based on the visual evidence of the desiccated and dead leaf is Die_Back.
